raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`@replay_launches` (#43859) replays a Triton wrapper's launches through `compiled[grid](*args)`, which is Triton's per-call runner. In Triton 3.7, `knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook` and `launch_exit_hook` are `HookChain` objects and are never `None`. So on every launch the runner:
- builds a `LazyDict` of launch metadata;
- has the C launcher call into two empty Python hook chains.

That costs about 2 µs per launch on an x86 host. It is now one of the larger pieces of a replayed call.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/common/fast_launch.py`:
- When no launch hook is registered, a replayed launch calls `compiled.run(...)` directly. It passes the current stream, exactly as the runner does, and no hook metadata.
- When a hook is registered (e.g. proton or another profiler), replay keeps going through the runner, so hooks still see every launch.
- The launcher handles (`run`, `function`, `packed_metadata`) are read when the plan is built. If Triton's compiled-kernel API moves, `_record`'s existing guard therefore leaves that signature on the normal path instead of failing at replay.

No memory is involved, and the recording path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- New test `test_launch_hooks_see_replayed_launches`: a hook registered on `knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook` sees the replayed launch.
- On H200:
  - `test_fast_launch.py` 33 passed;
  - `test_norm.py` 254 passed;
  - `test_layernorm_modulate.py` 21 passed;
  - `test_activation.py` 10 passed;
  - `test_flux2_strided_qknorm_rope.py` 2 passed (9 subtests);
  - `test_model_fast_paths.py` 97 passed, 1 skipped.
- End to end, output image md5 matched main in every configuration below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `f7ad4345b8`, torch 2.13, triton 3.7.1, H200 (Xeon 8558P), with processes pinned to the GPU's NUMA node.

**Host time per call** of each replayed wrapper in `test_fast_launch.WRAPPERS` (µs, inference mode; the GPU is kept busy so only submission is timed):

| wrapper | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `flux2_qknorm_rope` | 17.93 | 16.40 |
| `layernorm_modulate` | 14.18 | 12.77 |
| `layernorm_modulate_scale_only` | 13.44 | 11.77 |
| `packed_silu_mul` | 11.04 | 9.73 |
| `rmsnorm_scale` | 13.57 | 11.90 |
| `rmsnorm_tanh_residual` | 14.52 | 12.93 |
| `rope_rotate_half` | 15.04 | 13.50 |
| `silu_mul` | 13.79 | 12.21 |
| `zimage_qk_rmsnorm` | 12.49 | 11.10 |

**End to end.** On H200, two identical main servers resident together differed by 3.5% in an A/A run at Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512², which is as large as this change. So both paths were built into one server and chosen per request, and requests rotated through the arms in the same process. An extra base arm in each round measures in-process noise. Values are client wall-clock medians, eager:

| | vs base | faster than base in | in-process A/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512² | −2.4% | 7/10 | +0.5% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 1024² (GPU-bound) | +0.1% | 2/10 | +0.1% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512² | −2.1% | 8/8 | −0.4% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512², together with #44478 | −3.9% | 8/8 | |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1 GPU 512² | −0.3% | 13/16 | −0.2% |

Output images are unchanged: the same kernels are launched with the same arguments. The gain shows wherever the host bounds the step, and more so on Grace hosts (GB200/GB300), where the same Python costs roughly twice as much. No GB300 was available for this run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
